significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that an internal effect signal tracks the backdoor-adjusted effect across confounding strength, including the correct "dose-response sign-crossing," while an "adjustment" direction causally moves predictions toward the do-calculus answer; this combines a form-(iii) predictive coupling with a form-(ii) causal intervention. It would fix expected internal responses for previously untested confounding strengths and establish both a selective phenomenon—the "confounder-in-vs-out sign-flip" only in Simpson cases—and a mechanism connecting that representation to predictions, an important distinction because TabPFN's general predictive success (Hollmann et al., Nature 2025) does not itself license interventional interpretation. The negative branch would rule out usable backdoor adjustment in the tested models rather than merely report an absent probe, and true versus false are determinate through whether the signal follows the adjusted effect, crosses at the correct threshold, and supports selective steering. In the topic-substitution check, the generic question of whether scientific mechanisms are represented would not merit this score; the extra weight comes specifically from the claimed quantitative coupling and causal-use criterion.

reach.justification: The reusable handles are explicitly named as the "Adjustment-Beyond-Observational Index," "Confounder-In-vs-Out Flip Asymmetry," "interventional-fidelity dose-response," and a steerable "adjustment direction." These can function ex ante as a model-capability screen before causal-effect use—supporting the claimed "trust calibration" or gating of treatment-effect applications—while the steering direction is an inference-time intervention; likely downstream users therefore include model auditors and scientific-FM practitioners, not only mechanistic-interpretability researchers. After per-model re-extraction, the dose-response claim predicts a relation and sign-crossing rather than merely supplying a search procedure, although the substantive pass/fail finding is principally scoped to TabPFN and related tabular/scientific models and must be re-established for substantially different architectures or modalities. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: a generic scientific-representation claim supplies neither these auditing handles nor their pre-use action window.
